title: Constructive simplicial model with univalent universes
formal: Does the constructive set theory \(\mathsf S\) specified below support a full simplicial interpretation of intensional Martin-Löf type theory with \(0,1,\mathbb N,\Pi,\Sigma,\mathsf{Id}\) and a cumulative sequence of univalent universes, in which every type former, term former and eliminator is strictly stable under substitution? The required universes classify the small Kan fibrations between cofibrant Kan complexes described below. Work in CZF with a sequence \((I_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}\) of constructive inaccessible sets, \(I_i\in I_{i+1}\), and the explicit small-subset principle \[\forall i\ \forall a,b\; (a\subseteq b\ \land\ b\in I_i\ \Rightarrow\ a\in I_i).\] Do not assume excluded middle or an axiom of choice. This is the full-model target selected by the user on 16 September2026; a univalent fibration with only weakly stable type operations is insufficient.

source_formulation.text: Construct a constructive simplicial model of dependent type theory with univalent universes.

why: Simplicial sets provide a standard geometric language for homotopy theory and classical univalent semantics. A constructive full model would connect that language with foundations that track how mathematical objects are built. The unresolved coherence and size issues determine whether partial semantic structures actually interpret dependent type-theoretic substitution and universes.

sentences: The question asks for a constructive simplicial interpretation of dependent type theory with univalent universes.
The selected metatheory is CZF with a sequence of constructive inaccessible sets and the explicit principle that every subset of a small set is small.
The model must interpret the stated dependent type formers and make all operations commute strictly with substitution.
Existing constructive simplicial work provides substantial weakly stable structure but leaves the strict coherence issue open in the checked sources.
A full construction would connect simplicial homotopy theory with constructive univalent foundations without importing excluded middle or choice.

definitions:
The metatheory \(\mathsf S\) is intuitionistic first-order set theory CZF, together with the displayed sequence and small-subset axioms. CZF has Extensionality, Pairing, Union, Infinity, Set Induction, bounded Separation, Strong Collection and Subset Collection. Bounded Separation forms subsets using formulas whose quantifiers are all bounded by sets. Strong Collection says that if every \(x\in a\) has some \(y\) satisfying \(\varphi(x,y)\), there is a set \(b\) containing a witness for every such \(x\), with every element of \(b\) witnessing some \(x\in a\). Subset Collection can equivalently be given as Fullness: for sets \(a,b\), there is a set of total relations from \(a\) to \(b\) such that every total relation contains one in that set. A total relation from \(a\) to \(b\) is a subset of \(a\times b\) with a related element of \(b\) for each element of \(a\). Neither unrestricted Separation nor Power Set, excluded middle, countable choice or dependent choice is an additional axiom here. Ordinary consequences of the stated axioms remain available.

The word inaccessible uses the constructive set convention of Aczel–Rathjen. A set \(I\) is regular if it is inhabited and transitive, and whenever \(a\in I\) and \(R\subseteq a\times I\) is a total relation, there is a \(b\in I\) such that \[\forall x\in a\ \exists y\in b\ (xRy),\qquad\forall y\in b\ \exists x\in a\ (xRy).\] It is inaccessible if, in addition, \(\omega\in I\), it is closed under unions and under intersections of inhabited families that are elements of \(I\), and it satisfies internal Fullness: for every \(a,b\in I\), some \(C\in I\) is internally a full set of total relations from \(a\) to \(b\). Internally means that all quantifiers in this assertion are restricted to \(I\), using the inherited membership relation. Explicitly, its members are total subrelations of \(a\times b\), and each total relation \(R\in I\) contains one of them. This is a constructive inaccessible set, not a silently imported classical inaccessible cardinal. The whole sequence is supplied as one function on \(\omega\). A set is \(i\)-small if it belongs to \(I_i\). The small-subset principle quantifies over sets \(a\), not over arbitrary classes whose existence as sets is not given.

The simplex category \(\Delta\) has objects \([n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}\), \(n\ge0\), and order-preserving functions. A simplicial set is a functor \(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Set}\): sets \(X_n\) with restriction maps for every such function, satisfying identity and composition laws. Its morphisms are natural transformations. The standard simplex \(\Delta[n]\) has \(\Delta[n]_k=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([k],[n])\). The horn \(\Lambda^r[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]\), for \(n\ge1\) and \(0\le r\le n\), is the union of all codimension-one faces except the \(r\)-th. A Kan fibration \(p:E\to B\) has a specified diagonal filler for every commuting square with left map \(\Lambda^r[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]\). A Kan complex is a simplicial set whose map to the one-point simplicial set has this structure. Existence of fillers cannot be converted to a chosen filler operation by unmentioned choice.

A simplex is degenerate if it is the image of a simplex in smaller dimension under a degeneracy map, corresponding to a nonidentity surjection in \(\Delta\). Cofibrant means that degeneracy of each simplex is decidable, the constructive Kan–Quillen cofibrancy condition for an object. A simplicial set is \(i\)-small if each \(X_n\in I_i\). A map is \(i\)-small if each degreewise fiber belongs to \(I_i\). These notions supply the universe sizes. Contexts are represented by cofibrant Kan complexes, substitutions by simplicial maps, dependent types by Kan fibrations with cofibrant total space, and terms by sections. Auxiliary data for chosen fillers, codes and coherent pullbacks are permitted; the underlying families must still be simplicial fibrations. The construction need not use one predetermined presentation of the partial model in the sources.

A full interpretation provides a category with families: for each context \(\Gamma\), types over \(\Gamma\), terms of those types, substitution actions, an empty context and context extension \(\Gamma.A\) with its projection and generic term. A section of \(\Gamma.A\to\Gamma\) represents a term. For every substitution \(\sigma:\Delta\to\Gamma\), the chosen interpretation of \(A[\sigma]\) and the associated square over \(\sigma\) realize pullback. Reindexing satisfies \(A[\mathrm{id}]=A\), \(A[\sigma][\tau]=A[\sigma\circ\tau]\), and the corresponding term equalities as equalities of chosen data, not merely through unspecified isomorphisms. Additional context-extension data may be used to achieve these equalities.

The object theory is intensional dependent type theory with empty and unit types, natural numbers, dependent functions \(\Pi\), dependent pairs \(\Sigma\) and identity types \(\mathsf{Id}_A(a,b)\). It has their formation, introduction and full dependent elimination rules, with judgmental beta computation for application, projections, natural-number recursion and identity elimination at reflexivity. The empty type has elimination into every type; the unit type has its usual dependent eliminator. Function and pair eta may be propositional; no judgmental eta rule is imposed as an extra target. There is no equality reflection or uniqueness-of-identity-proofs axiom. Empty, unit and natural-number types are interpreted by the corresponding discrete simplicial sets, with the usual distinct numerals and recursion. Identity types have the homotopy-theoretic path-object interpretation and the dependent identity eliminator; they are not interpreted using proof-irrelevant equality in the metatheory.

For each \(i\), a universe is a chosen fibration \(\widetilde U_i\to U_i\) with \(i\)-small fibers. It classifies \(i\)-small Kan fibrations between the specified cofibrant Kan complexes: each such family is, up to an isomorphism of families, a pullback along a code map into \(U_i\). Universes themselves have codes at the next level. Chosen inclusions of codes implement cumulativity and preserve their decoded families; there is no universe that contains itself. At every level, the universe contains codes for \(0,1,\mathbb N\) and is closed under the stated \(\Pi,\Sigma,\mathsf{Id}\) operations in arbitrary contexts, not just contexts made of small types.

Univalence requires that the canonical map from identity of two universe codes to equivalence of their decoded types is itself an equivalence. An equivalence is a function whose fibers are contractible; a type is contractible if it has a point and a path from that point to every other point. These are the internal type-theoretic notions, interpreted simplicially. All type constructors, terms, eliminators, universe codes, decoding operations and univalence witnesses must commute with substitution as equalities of the chosen interpretation. Their required judgmental computation rules must hold as equalities as well. Having operations that commute only up to isomorphism, homotopy or weak equivalence does not meet this strict stability condition.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete Lean-checked construction and verification of this full simplicial interpretation using only the specified constructive metatheory and size axioms, or a complete Lean-checked impossibility theorem for that target. The formalization must make the metatheoretic assumptions explicit: either represent derivations in \(\mathsf S\), or give an interpretation parametrized by a model of \(\mathsf S\) whose construction uses exactly its permitted reasoning. Lean's ambient classical choice or excluded middle cannot silently prove a step required internally in \(\mathsf S\). A positive answer must verify all universe, substitution and computation conditions, including arbitrary-context dependent-product closure. A weakly stable comprehension category, an isolated univalent classifying fibration, a classical simplicial model or a constructive model solely in cubical sets is insufficient. A negative answer must concern the full allowed simplicial target, not merely show that one existing coherence construction fails. No additional higher inductive types or normalization theorem is requested.

context_blocks.text: The historical source asks broadly for a constructive simplicial model with univalent universes. On 16 September2026 the user selected CZF with a sequence of constructive inaccessible sets, the small-subset principle and a full strictly substitution-stable interpretation. This makes the metatheory and model requirements explicit; it does not replace the question by one theorem about a particular existing construction.

Gambino–Henry construct identity, sum, product and basic inductive type structure and a univalent universe in a comprehension category of cofibrant simplicial sets. Their Theorem8.1 labels the stability of these operations separately: some are pseudo-stable, products are weakly stable and identity elimination has a remaining stability qualification.

Remark8.5 leaves the passage to a strict model open. The standard cited coherence theorem has a hypothesis that fails in their constructive setting because cofibrant objects need not be closed under categorical dependent products. This is a limitation of that available coherence argument, not a theorem excluding every full constructive simplicial model.

The partial construction explicitly uses the additional principle that subsets of small sets are small when establishing universe closure under arbitrary dependent products. Remark8.3 gives weaker alternatives without it. The selected target allows this principle and therefore should not be described as the stronger no-resizing problem.

The 2026 equivariant cubical-model paper still describes the strictness gap in the constructive simplicial account. It separately discusses effective Kan fibrations, whose required universes and complete interpretation are not established in that comparison. Its own cubical construction has a different underlying category.

The 2025 presentation and May2026 higher-sheaf preprint describe constructive cubical developments and a base construction announced as forthcoming. They do not by themselves provide a checked strict interpretation with the specified simplicial families and size assumptions.

Constructive inaccessible sets are regular sets with additional closure and internal Fullness properties. Giving this definition matters because a classical inaccessible cardinal imports a different background theory. The separate small-subset axiom is recorded independently rather than being hidden inside the word inaccessible.
